phases.title: Phase 1: Extract outer API layer (1 module)
phases.strategy: Place API Gateway in front. Route new requests to extracted microservice; legacy endpoints stay live until traffic shifts.
phases.rollback: Switch API Gateway route back to legacy endpoints
phases.rationale: Controllers are the outermost layer — they hold routing and input validation but no persistent state. Extracting them first lets us place a gateway over the legacy monolith and start splitting traffic. Scope: 1 module(s), 9,955 LOC, 52 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 2: Extract shared domain models (1 module)
phases.strategy: Extract domain entities into a shared contracts package consumed by both the legacy app and the new service.
phases.rollback: Revert contracts package version; legacy model remains authoritative
phases.rationale: Domain models are the contracts between caller and callee. Lifting them into a shared package unblocks parallel work on the dependent services. Scope: 1 module(s), 5,400 LOC, 0 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 3: Extract data access layer (1 module)
phases.strategy: Introduce an anti-corruption layer over the legacy DB. New service reads via views; writes flow through the legacy path until the schema is owned by the new service.
phases.rollback: Remove anti-corruption layer; reads/writes resume on legacy schema
phases.rationale: Data access is high risk because schema changes require coordination with every consumer. We use an anti-corruption layer to decouple the new service from legacy SQL. Scope: 1 module(s), 10,700 LOC, 96 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 4: Untangle shared legacy libraries (1 module)
phases.strategy: Identify consumers and lift the shared module into a versioned package. Extract one consumer at a time; deprecate the shared copy once all consumers migrate.
phases.rollback: Restore shared library import; republish legacy version
phases.rationale: Shared libraries are the hardest to extract — every consumer is affected. We handle them after leaf modules are stable so we can migrate consumers one at a time. Scope: 1 module(s), 3,846 LOC, 197 known vulnerabilities.

phases.title: Phase 5: Wrap mainframe components (1 module)
phases.strategy: DO NOT rewrite. Wrap mainframe programs with a thin API adapter (REST or message queue) so new services consume them as dependencies. Plan replacement only after all callers migrate.
phases.rollback: Remove API adapter; clients resume direct JCL calls
phases.rationale: Mainframe programs are expensive to rewrite and carry decades of business rules. We wrap them behind an API and treat them as dependencies until replacement is justified by a separate business case. Scope: 1 module(s), 261 LOC, 0 known vulnerabilities.

narrative: The app-05 application contains 6 modules (30,281 lines of code, 345 known vulnerabilities). NexusForge proposes a 5-phase strangler decomposition covering controller, mainframe, model, repository, shared. Total estimated effort: 91 engineer-days (~18 working weeks for a single engineer, or ~4 weeks for a 4-engineer team working in parallel). Each phase is independently deployable and reversible — no big-bang cut-over.
